summary: The diff does what the task and the agreed decisions ask. In index.html the five save/sync elements (📓 Save to workbook, #btn-wb-sync, #btn-wb-cloud, #wb-cloud-where, #btn-save-all-modified) moved out of header .header-actions into #wb-save-sync-row, a direct child of <body> placed between </header> and <div class="toolbar">. That puts it outside #toolbar-groups, so the ☰ collapse never hides it. Their ids, onclick/oncontextmenu handlers, data-i/data-i-title keys and titles are byte-identical, and the ☁ button still has no data-i, so paintCloud() still owns its label. The order is unchanged and the status text sits right after ☁. The old tablet rules (display:contents on desktop, order:-1/width:100% inside the header) are replaced by one base rule: flex, nowrap, overflow-x:auto, left-aligned, var(--surface) and var(--border) tokens, no hex. The breakpoints only change padding. `.wb-save-sync-row .btn { flex: 0 0 auto; white-space: nowrap }` (specificity 0,2,0) beats the phone rule `.btn { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0 }`, so the buttons neither squash nor wrap. #wb-cloud-where keeps its nowrap/ellipsis styling and is flex 0 0 auto, so a long status makes the row scroll instead of breaking. The comments describing the old placement are rewritten; docs/FEATURES.md § E/§ O now name the row; tests/gdsync.js's placement selector is updated. MAP.md has no anchors for the header markup, so there was nothing to move there. I re-ran the checks myself: `node tests/verify.js` passes (JS parses, all nine nav blocks synced, diacritics OK); the tester's row.js passes 23/23 (structure, order, one-line geometry from 1920 px down to 360 px and landscape phone, sideways scroll, ☰ collapse, theme parity, RO/EN, Ctrl+S/Ctrl+Alt+S, clicks); `tests/gdsync.js` passes fully. The tester reports idea.js and nav.js show only their known CLAUDE.md failures. I would merge this.
